text:
Two separate systems here — a session memory (notes) and a corpus (self-improvement data) — and they have opposite requirements. Notes must be cheap, mutable, disposable; corpus data must be curated, measured, permanent. Keep them apart or the corpus fills with noise.

Notes: cross-context handoff
Attach notes to the oracle's phase state, scoped to the model:

Bash
tools/seat oracle note "doors intentionally unwelded — articulation; hinge line at x=0.82"
tools/seat oracle note --decision "dropped underbody detail per user, budget spent on fascia"
tools/seat oracle status
# → { phase, checks, notes:[{at, generation, text, kind:"decision"|"observation"|"todo"}] }
Three disciplines make notes actually useful instead of a stale-context trap:

Notes record intent, never facts derivable from the percept. "Hood bbox is 1.2m" is poison — the next agent trusts it after three edits changed it. "User wants the hood asymmetric, don't mirror it" is exactly right: it's the one thing look can never tell a cold agent. Enforce this in the phase doc: if the seat can measure it, don't write it down.
Stamp every note with the generation it was written at. oracle status marks notes from older generations as possibly-stale automatically. A cold agent reads decisions as durable and observations as suspect — same three-horizon honesty as semantic-status.
The handoff story becomes: cold agent runs oracle status → gets phase, live host-verified checks, and the previous agent's decisions. Position from measurement, intent from notes. Nothing about "where was I" depends on the previous context window having summarized itself well.
The corpus: what to log, automatically
You're already generating the training data; you just aren't keeping it structured. Per session, per model:

Oracle trajectory: phases entered, checks failed and how many attempts to pass, refusals hit, undo density per phase. This tells you where agents struggle — a check that fails 4× average across sessions is either badly specified or missing a supporting verb.
Escape hatches (the bun/jq/sleep greps) — already discussed, but log them into the same store.
Follow transcripts + their distilled recipes, with the approve/reject outcome.
Final model metrics from the audit machinery, keyed to whether the model was accepted — this is the labeled dataset the class-spec idea needs.
Class specs: the car screenshot, as data
Your screenshot is the key insight made visible. That car is a spec — every load-bearing decision is measurable from the package:

Bash
tools/seat oracle spec car
# → derived from N approved exemplars:
# { triangles: {median: 3400, p90: 5200},          # PS2-era, as numbers not vibes
#   quadRatio: {min: 0.85},
#   dimensions: {length:[3.8,4.6], height:[1.3,1.6]},
#   parts: {median: 12,
#     articulation: ["ds_front_door","ps_front_door","ds_rear_door","ps_rear_door",
#                    "front_hood_lid","trunk_lid","front_bumper","rear_bumper"],
#     welded: ["body shell — one component"]},
#   matingFacesKept: "articulation parts only",     # doors keep their jamb faces
#   namingPattern: {sides:"ds_/ps_", regions:[8,15]},
#   densityMap: "high at fascia/wheel arches, sparse on roof/floor" }
Notice what the Outliner in your image encodes: the part list is the articulation spec. Doors, lids, bumpers are separate parts because they open or break — which is exactly your existing rule for when mating faces legitimately survive. A class spec turns "keep mating faces on parts that articulate" from a judgment call into a lookup: for class car, these eight junctions stay separate, everything else welds. The vertex-density gradient visible in the wireframe (dense fascia, sparse roof) is equally extractable — edge-length statistics per region across exemplars.

Then the oracle binds it end to end:

Bash
tools/seat oracle start "build a compact sedan"
# → classifies as car, loads the spec, and now:
#   - scale check: bbox vs class dimensions (kills the 4×-oversized trap per-class)
#   - budget check: tri count vs class p90, warned DURING blockout not at the end
#   - finish gate: articulation parts from the spec exempt from junction resolution;
#     everything else must weld
#   - naming check: ds_/ps_ convention, region count in class range
"PS2-era depth" stops being something an agent must infer from a phrase and becomes the distribution it's being graded against.

The self-improvement loop, staged honestly
Now: you hand-pick exemplars (this car, Van_Seat, radio_001). oracle spec runs the audit machinery over them at curation time and caches the profile. Human-gated: only models you mark approved enter the corpus — an unguarded corpus converges on average agent output, which is exactly the 43%-unreachable disease you're curing.
Soon: every accepted agent-built model is offered into the corpus; you approve or reject. Rejections with reasons are the most valuable rows — they become new checks.
Later: check-failure statistics propose spec refinements ("agents pass quad-ratio but the accepted cars cluster at 0.9, not the 0.85 floor — tighten?"), and Follow demonstrations that repeatedly correct the same class-specific mistake get distilled into class-scoped recipes (car-wheel-arch).
Eventually: oracle start "build a car like these three" takes model ids as exemplars directly and derives a one-off spec — which is your end-state: the agent looks at examples and reads the required depth, because depth was always just measurements it now has verbs for.
resolution: Built the two memories as two systems that never touch, because they have opposite requirements. Notes (seatNotes.ts) are cheap, mutable, disposable and per-model: they ride the model package as notes.json so a cold agent reads the previous agent's intent and deleting the model deletes them, with an in-memory fallback that reports durable:false for an unsaved model. Two disciplines are enforced — intent only, stated in the setup and finish phase docs as 'if the seat can measure it, do not write it down', and generation stamping so decisions stay durable while observations and todos go suspect the moment the mesh advances. The class corpus (seatClassSpec.ts) is the opposite: curated, measured, permanent, human-gated. oracle spec derives a target distribution from approved exemplars, and the key result is that a finished model's part list IS its articulation spec — derived live from Compact_Car_001 it recovered the ds_/ps_ front and rear doors, front_hood_lid, trunk_lid and both bumpers, which turns 'keep the mating faces articulation can expose' from a judgement call into a lookup. Class criteria grade during blockout rather than at the end so the oversized and over-budget traps are caught before detail exists, bounds widen by a tolerance, and a one-exemplar spec carries a caveat. Approval requires --by and an agent cannot self-approve. Telemetry (seatTelemetry.ts) logs every refusal so a check that needs re-specifying or a supporting verb surfaces as a number, and rejection reasons are kept because each is a check that does not exist yet. Verified live end to end; all four suites green.
